# C202 ? diagnosis only; no production fix accepted

**C202 is NOT complete. Do not integrate an animation fix from this branch: it contains none.**
The required source-level correction, unchanged-good-join positive control, default-OFF switch,
and successful before/after acceptance have not been achieved. This branch preserves the
reproduction and the rejected controls instead of shipping the forbidden floating-pelvis workaround.

## Diagnosis, before proposing a fix

The two cited windows are not simply hook/reaction blends. Replaying the original career
fighters and seed on the fetched tree shows a hook and locomotion in the first window,
and rapidly changing locomotion/idle takes in the second. No `react_*` take is current in
either exact 40?45 or 65?70 second interval of this replay. The room's last-event text is
not the AnimationPlayer's current clip; the instrument reads the latter.

The deep hook bend exists in the unblended source. At source t=0.866667,
`H2H_HookPunch_InPlace.FBX` pelvis Y is 0.763861 m and knee included angles are
123.421/122.156 degrees. Retargeted f01 has 123.459/122.077 degrees and its pelvis is
0.821249 m above the arena mat. At that frame animation sample, body layer, inertia,
layer-hips join, foot lock, grounding and final contact output agree on pelvis height.
The source-to-target comparison does not support a doubled carry or a retargeted knee collapse.
It does not establish that the source movement is artistically acceptable.

Plain crossfade and foot-lock-off do not remove the deep poses. Hip-carry-off raises the
hook pelvis from 0.821249 to 1.035352 m but leaves knees at 123.459/122.077 degrees;
toes rise from 0.017964/0.019280 to 0.232066/0.233382 m above the mat. This is the task's
floating-body trap, reproduced as a rejected diagnostic arm, not a production switch.
It also lifts an ordinary idle, so it fails the unchanged-good-join condition.

A safe next intervention needs coherent support-foot/leg/pelvis authoring or an explicitly
approved replacement source for the offending standing motions. Merely shortening the
hook is not demonstrated safe: its 0.567-second recovery still has pelvis 0.852 m above
the mat, and its intact 1.0-second endpoint returns to guard. No arbitrary crop, vertical
clamp, or idle lower-body substitution is shipped. These measurements reject the tested
mechanisms; they do not prove that no other valid source fix is possible.

and camera_keep_pair ON. Same configuration in all four arms; no event reduction.
Original plan's BEGIN FIGHT is frame 787 at 30 Hz (26.233333 s); its full count is 2719
frames / 90.633333 s, matching C198's recording. Tables report nominal original-video
seconds as 26.233333 + elapsed bout seconds. This is the deterministic replay mapping,

Both requested windows are measured on the current tree, each at 30 Hz, both fighters,
seven writer stages. Final census is 1800 frames, 25200 writer-stage rows per arm.
All 3600 per-fighter clip-name/clock tuples (1800 frames x two fighters) match the before
arm in each of crossfade/nofoot/nohip. This is clock parity, not the unachieved

`hips_m` subtracts FightWorldLiveScreen._live_deck_y, the arena's actual surface,
not a guessed ground or the skeleton's toe plane. Knee angle is hip?knee?ankle included
angle (180 degrees means straight). Early exploratory numbers used the toe plane;
only the corrected mat-relative values below are acceptance evidence.

## Guard reference and failed acceptance

Floor definition: minimum pelvis height in the full retargeted RamsterZ `H2H_Idle.FBX`
0.00?4.67 s window, sampled at 30 Hz on the mounted body with no procedural writers.
It is **0.954191 m for f01 and 0.914841 m for f02**, both minima at t=0.300 s.
This is a sourced guard reference, not a universal biomechanical minimum: the authored
hook, locomotion and slip clips legitimately contain lower source keys. A requirement
that every standing exchange remain above that idle floor is **not met** by these assets
or by the crossfade/foot-lock controls. No claim of floor compliance is made.

## Clip ownership and join modes

- `hook_lead`: H2H_HookPunch_InPlace.FBX, whole source 0.00?1.00 s; current take starts
  at nominal video 41.366667, ends into idle at 42.333333. Low point at 42.200000 is
  clip t=0.866667, after the entry inertial decay, not at a reaction join.
- `loc_strafe_right`: H2H_WalkRight.FBX, loop 0.00?1.00 s. B's low point is at
  40.300000, t=0.195130. A's low point in the second interval is 67.700000,
  t=0.189612. The latter is inside a locomotion join, but crossfade retains the drop.
- `loc_retreat_right`: H2H_WalkBackRight.FBX, loop 0.00?1.00 s; B enters at
  67.633333, t=0.095104, already inheriting a low locomotion pose.
- Before: caller-clock inertia, strike and stance joins 0.27 s; reaction head/neck
  snap 0.05 s with limb/hip decay 0.27 s (no reactions in these two intervals).
- Crossfade control: inertialization disabled through the existing measurement option;
  ordinary strike blend 0.10 s / stance 0.20 s. Nofoot disables existing foot lock only.
  Nohip resets animation Hips translation keys to the body's rest origin in the tool
  process only. Production animations and runtime scripts remain untouched.

## Reproduce

Parse both tools first. Run `tools/c202_probe.gd` headless with `-- arm=before`, then
`arm=crossfade`, `arm=nofoot`, `arm=nohip`. Run `tools/c202_source.gd` for source/FK
comparisons. JSON output goes to `.godot/c202/`; no raw source asset is rewritten.
For video, use Tools/godot_hidden.ps1 with the probe, --rendering-method gl_compatibility,
--rendering-driver opengl3, --fixed-fps 30, --resolution 854x480, and user arguments
`arm=before record=true` or `arm=crossfade record=true`. Encode the 420 numbered PNGs
from `.godot/c202/<arm>_frames` at 30 fps, scaling to 854:480. The filename counter
concatenates the two bounded windows; simulation itself runs continuously for 60 s.
